utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. The next witness is Muharem Besic. MR. MUHAREM BESIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, would you please take the oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may be seated. Examined by MR. TIEGER

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Sir, what is your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muharem Besic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what year were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 12th October 1955 in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend elementary school in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that at Rade Kondic school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were a young adult, did you work in Zagreb for approximately three or four years as a painter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time did you return home to Kozarac every week or two to spend the weekend?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there then a two-year period when you were back living in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then a couple of years after that when you worked in construction in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period of time as well did you return home to spend the weekends in Kozarac every other week or so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that you returned to live and work in Kozarac full time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So with the exception of those four or five years in Croatia during which you were coming home regularly, you lived in Kozarac your whole life until the conflict in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you living in Kozarac immediately before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in the village of Besici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With whom did you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Besici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you reside there with your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived with my father, mother, brother, his wife and two of his children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, do you know Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I have known him since early childhood, since I was 10 or 12, so that is about 30 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the two of you go to school together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know each other by nicknames?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you call him and what did he call you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I called him Dule and he called me Cicak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you remain on sociable terms with Dusko Tadic as you grew up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we were not particularly close, but whenever we met we would greet each other, "Hello, Dule, what's new?" and things like that and the same he asked of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you associate together at times, for example, sitting in cafes having drinks and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did. We were often in company together, well, perhaps not often, perhaps once a year, perhaps not even that much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know his parents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His brothers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His brothers, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you good friends with any of his brothers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With his elder brother, Ljubo, we were very close for about two years. We were true friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you visit the Tadic home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with his elder brother, Ljubo, I used to go to his home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Tadic's wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, after the beginning of the war in Croatia and increasing tensions between Muslims and Serbs, did you observe some of the people who gathered in Mr. Tadic's cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In particular, were persons who were supporters of the war and involved in it frequent patrons of Mr. Tadic's cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, people who -----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could my learned friend not lead in relation to such matters as he is inviting the witness to support the conclusion within his question?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The question was, in particular, who were supporters of the war. I am trying to look at the question. If it is just preliminary, then there is no problem. Mr. Tieger, what was the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe the question was, were persons who were supporters of the war and involved in it frequent patrons of Mr. Tadic's cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will overrule the objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were frequent patrons of the cafe, those people who were waging war in Croatia, and who had come back from the front and those reservists. Those soldiers of those, they used to come quite often to this cafe and then drink into the late hours of the night and did all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some of those persons residents of the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember some of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Drago Vidovic called "Tepo", Goran Borovnica and many other people whose names I did not know. They came by army vehicles and they parked there. I could see it very well because across the street was the barber's shop where I was every day, rather, every second day, to get a shave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those persons whose names you did not know who came by army vehicles, were those persons from outside the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From around Kozarac because there were no such people in the centre of Kozarac or, at least, very few of them but from the area of Kozarac, from the broader area of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, were you in Kozarac when the military attack began on May 24th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in central Kozarac at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was in the centre of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you seek shelter in the basement of the bank which was located on the main street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was, yes. I did. I was in the cellar of the bank together with the people from that building and inhabitants of the adjacent building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you essentially remain there until you surrendered to Serb forces on May 26th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I stayed there until Tuesday morning around 9.00 or 10 o'clock, I would not know exactly, when the column was formed in front of the bank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a column. What was at the head of this column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the head of the column, that was the order, it was in, I do not know who ordered it, but that white flag should be carried and there was a boy with a white flag at the head of the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the column consist of Muslim men, women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the population of Kozarac, even the new borns were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the situation in Kozarac at this time? What did central Kozarac look like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you know, the roofs had already been shelled. There were fires here and there, but mostly roofs and windows had already been broken, shattered, by detonations and the trees, when a shell would hit a tree, then the road was quite green with branches and leaves. So, Kozarac was shelled from Sunday at 2 o'clock and for two days and then it was very intensive shelling. The shelling went as if a sewing machine was sewing seeds in the field and that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, where did the column go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The column moved towards the Prijedor/Banja Luka road or, rather, we were told to head for Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the column stop at some point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The column stopped at the first stop towards, on the way towards Prijedor, in Sujica at a stop called Limenka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said the first stop, by that you mean the first bus stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that was the first time that we stopped as pedestrians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how far away is that from the junction of the Prijedor/Banja Luka road and the road to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About a kilometre and a half or two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were Serb forces there at Limenka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were lots of military there, tanks, armoured vehicles, guns, cannons, machine gunnists. They were all armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say there were lots of military there. How were the Serbs dressed? What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of them wore camouflage uniforms, so they had some hats here with some flaps. There were also some people who had masks over their faces. Some had their face open. There were people who had half civilian, half military clothes on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these persons in uniform armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course, they were all armed with rifles, some even had machine guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At Limenka were Muslim men separated from the Muslim women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were separated. Men were separated from women and then once again men were separated again, that is, some were boarded on some buses and others on other buses. I do not know what that particular separation meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some Muslim men taken to places other than the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, across the street from Limenka on the left-hand side in the direction of Prijedor, there was a very big house with a balcony the length of that building, and there was the machine gun turned towards the road, towards us. There were some four or five Serb soldiers on that balcony and people were being taken into that building. Among others there was some called Muma. I do not know his surname because he did not live for a long time in Kozarac. He was married to a Kozarac woman and lived there, but otherwise he came from Prijedor. He was taken in, amongst others. As far as I could judge, the situation there must have been in that house somebody who knew Kozarac and Kozarac people very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were the men who were taken into that house ever seen again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, neither heard nor seen them alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you placed on a bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was first separated from the column as such that was taken with men, and then, as something special, I was taken on to a bus and they were searched by Serb policemen, let me in and took down my name and surname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that did your bus leave the area of Limenka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The bus started towards Prijedor in the direction of Prijedor. We stopped in Kozarusa across Ziko's coffee bar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After stopping at Ziko's coffee bar, did the bus proceed on to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the bus continued towards Prijedor, but we then did go toward to Keraterm because it is before Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the men on the bus unloaded and held in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we got off the bus. We had to lower our hands like this at the back of the head and we entered a building in Keraterm which was very dusty, and there were lots of packaging materials there, pallets and things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you held in Keraterm, in what part of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a large room. Before it there is a small narrow room and then comes this large one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you spend that night in Keraterm and the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spent that night in Keraterm, the next day, and around 10 o'clock in the evening they began to load us on to buses again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were those buses taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I was to learn only after several hours on the bus. We were brought to Omarska, to the mine of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you arrived in Omarska sometime in the middle of the night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, could have been around midnight or one hour after midnight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were guards present to meet the buses when they arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the guards were standing in a cordon and we had to pass between them in order to reach that room in which we were then detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the prisoners have to leave the buses in any particular way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We had to have our hands up and pass between them, and they beat us with whatever they could lay their hands on, some more, some less, with a stick, if they had it, with a baton or with a kick of the foot and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you first held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were first confined in a huge room. What does it mean, "huge"? A large room. I should say, from what I could see since I had worked a lot in the field and changed my clothes on construction sites, they were lockers for clothes. I know what they look like. So this was a room where workers changed their clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, during the time you were in Omarska were prisoners killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the same night we did not even all come in, and only men with a strong character, somebody who really -- there was Ahil Dedic who had a very strong will, and they first beat him there at the entrance. Then Ahil came in and he was all beaten up and torn and then, in my estimate, after about 10 minutes and knowing him well, Ahil was crazy. He broke down one door and he found a piece of machinery, and then we were still not inmates, we were detainees, but when he broke down that door, you could hear the noise and a Serb soldier came in, that one called Cigo. I only know him by his nickname. He hit Ahil with a rifle butt across the face, with the butt. His barrel was in his arms. Then Ahil was taken out and then you could hear shots, a spray. I cannot say that he was killed, but the facts are talking about that because next morning I saw him lying on the grass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Ahil Dedic's corpse the next morning lying on the grass?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of Ahil Dedic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The day after you arrived, Mr. Besic, were you taken for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the next day a soldier came in and said to line up in fours and we would go to be interrogated, and I was in the first four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken for integration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to be interrogated upstairs in the building where the kitchen was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Upstairs, did you see any Serbs whom you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, up the spiral staircase going upstairs there were about maybe six, maybe up to 10 of them. I did not count them. I was not looking at them in their faces. My hands were behind my head and Neso Janjic said, "Where have you been, Cicak?" and I said, "Here I am". He is the only one I recognised. He had a cafe in Suhi Brod. It was called Sretno. It was not his ownership. He was just leasing it and he was from a village near Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you searched before you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was brought in front of a door and then they leaned me against a wall, my face against a wall, with three fingers up and then the soldier sort of felt me all around and when that was done, the door was open and I was led inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the person who interrogated you and did you know him before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I got in the man said, "Hello, Cicak". It was my acquaintance. We knew each other his name is Rade Knezevic. He was a former inspector of SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is Mr. Knezevic's nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After interrogation, Mr. Besic, where were you held then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After interrogation, I was taken to the garage. It is a small room in this huge room -- this huge building. As you come in, it is to the right from the door that I went in by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time it was about noon, and I was held there the whole night and the next day until dusk, sort of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other prisoners held there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as they were interrogated some were going to other rooms and some were coming to me in this garage. The garage filled up and we were all like stuck into the ground. You could not move. It was over 100 people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that you were held there the whole day and the next day until dusk. Where were you then moved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. Then we were taken, I was taken to that huge room, on the top floor, up the stairs, and then we were held for about an hour because it was overcrowded. Then they said the ones who were closest to the door, they would be taken elsewhere and I was among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you then taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to the ground floor in another room which was called the electric workshop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, I would like you in a moment to stand up and point out on the model the room in which you were held, the room you have just mentioned. When you get to that portion of the model, if you would put on the earphones which will be handed to you, and if you can take the pointer which is on the desk as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, if you are going to speak, if you will speak as in the direction of the microphone which is on the table to your right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point out for us then where you were taken after interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the interrogation I was taken in this room here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could return to that position there? That was the small garage you referred to, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The small garage, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you held after that? The cord has been disconnected. Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you well -- oh, I cannot hear anything now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you hear any sound now as it is being interpreted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot hear anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There may be a disconnection in the portion of the wire which is on the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just heard something. I just heard something. Can you repeat it? No, I cannot hear anything now -- yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry about the technical problem, sir. Can you hear me now? Mr. Besic, if I could ask you to pick up the pointer which is behind you on the model and can you either indicate or tell us where you were held immediately after you left the small garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, I am not getting any translation now.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are hearing it but in Serbo-Croat, not in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that I was taken to the top floor, the large room to the room that goes up the stairs to the top floor where I spent about one hour. As they were deciding, they took us back to this room downstairs that is called the electric workshop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read the number which is written which appears on the floor of the room in which you were held?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, did you normally stay in a particular part of that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. All the time I spent in this part here. That means the top left corner of the room, looking from the door as you walk in here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the Court able to see that and was counsel able to see the approximate position the witness indicated? Sir, if you could just point out your approximate spot once again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Besic, you can take your seat again. Thank you. Mr. Besic, can I ask you to briefly describe the general conditions in Omarska during the period of time you were held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What shall I tell you? For in 70, 75 days that I was there I lost 29 kilos. I was first weighed in Manjaca afterwards and this can be, sort of, supported by the Red Cross. I was not bathing. I was not having a hygiene and then I was not lying down stretched for a single night. There were a lot of lice. We were all tired. People were beaten up, people coming in. People urinated in the room. People even urinated with their clothes on. So you can imagine when people spent all day at 35, 40 centigrade, so you can imagine how it looked with 200 people in the room. The room is, maybe, let us say it is 40 square metres -- I think that is even too much -- but you can just imagine what was going on with us there. Then the people were sick and then people were weeping. For the first eight days, I was not even going out to eat. I was too afraid. I was -- I mentioned my nickname, Cicak. Everybody knew me as "Cicak". People did not know my name because I think that death was waiting for me, had I stepped out -- me and the others as well. What they said that it was just a centre, reception centre. That is a lie. There was no basis in that. The war was created because they followed -- a curse was following them. First, you have something, then you were taken everything away from you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, did you remain in Omarska until you were transferred to Manjaca in early August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I stayed there until August 6th in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have this photograph marked as Exhibit 268 for identification, please? Mr. Besic, do you recognise that photograph or what is shown in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the centre of this photograph it is me personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a picture taken in Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this photograph for admission and ask that it be placed on the Elmo.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 268 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, can you point out where you are, where you appear in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about how long after you arrived in Manjaca this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe about a month, a month and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Mr. Besic, did you ever see Dule Tadic in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the room where I spent all the time in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the room you pointed out to us on the model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the approximate date when you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact date, but it was summer in the range between 16th and 19th June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the approximate time of the day when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the afternoon somewhere around between 4.00 and 5.00, 4.00 and 5.00 there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That afternoon did you become generally aware that people from outside the camp were coming to your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, they were coming. The so-called coloured ones, that means the ones in the camouflage uniforms, and the ones who were coming from the front lines, and they were coming to some kind of furlough or something, and then as they would come in they would beat people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were prisoners particularly afraid of these people from outside the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For instance, the guards that were there, those were common people. You know, they just take them from their homes so that they be guards. Then they say, "Get inside, the coloured ones are coming", and whoever was -- they would just cower so they would not be exposed and the guards themselves feared them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did some prisoners who had been outside the room when these persons were thought to be coming to the camp come back to the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. There were people who were at that moment, for instance, they were on the toilet, I remember Senad Garibovic. I think that he is dead. I never saw him again. He was taken a few days later. He came back all wet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point after that did you hear prisoners being called from their rooms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when it all quietened down, they started calling out inmates, and I cannot give you the exact order. Eno Alic was called out, Emir Karabasic and Jasko Hrnic. Jasko Hrnic was called out last. He was with me in the same room. He was called out five or six times, and they called him "Asko" about five or six times and he would not respond. Then Dule Tadic came to the door and said, "Jasko, get out. I know you are in there. I will kill you all". And Jasko stood up and went to the door. As he was leaving, I saw Dusko Tadic. When Jasko opened the door, I could see Dusko Tadic clearly. It all lasted for about 10 seconds, maybe longer. I just looked up and saw who it was and I knew who Dule Tadic was because I knew his voice. I knew he was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, do you recall where Jasko Hrnic's place in the room was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Jasko's place was under the table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that table located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The table was just around the corner, left from the door about three metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before Jasko Hrnic left the room, did you hear sounds coming from outside the room which indicated what was happening to the other prisoners who had been called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, probably they had already come out, Eno Alic and Emir Karabasic. You could hear screams from pain and blows, like animal screams, as if they were not people any more, but animals. People can be like a horse, horses are being castrated. I do not know if I should explain how horses are being castrated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what Jasko Hrnic's condition was before he was called out? Had he been beaten previously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was beaten and he spent maybe 10 days in that small garage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where had he been before Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was caught on Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the numerous times that Jasko Hrnic was called out and he finally moved toward the door to get out, did he do anything before he left the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said something to the people around him and he put on as some sort of protection when he was going to be beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that Jasko was being called out before and not responding, was the door open or closed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Closed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The door was opened when Jasko finally left the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Jasko opened the door. At the very door there was a lot of people right around the door. They were almost on top of each other so that you could not just go straight to the door. You had to walk and avoid people's feet or hands or heads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long the door remained opened after Jasko left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When Jasko went out you could see Dule clearly and, as he was stepping over the doorstep, Dule cursed his mother and you could hear a blow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see the blow or just hear it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only heard it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what Dule Tadic was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic was wearing a camouflage uniform and maybe a beard of, you know, 10, 14 days, 12 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Jasko left the room, could you hear more sounds coming from the area of the hangar floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could hear a "Bite", a "Suck", "Where is your karate now?" Then screams "Hit him" and such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "screams", do you mean people shouting at the prisoners or prisoners crying out in pain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I suppose those were the people who are the perpetrators. I think that they were yelling, and I cannot tell you who it was that they were yelling at or shouting at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear the sounds of prisoners crying out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I already explained, as screams, people were screaming like animals, "Why me? What have I done to you?" It was all kinds -- you cannot imagine what situation it was like. It is in that moment, I do not know, we were about -- I am sure we were in this camp 3,000. I do not know if anybody was even breathing loudly, let alone listen. I think that it was all lasted for about an hour, somewhere around there, but I do not know if there is a single inmate in Omarska who did not have it up to here of all that. I do not think that there is a single man who does not remember that incident. I think that whoever mentions Omarska, every inmate thinks of that first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, the translation we received says that you heard a bite and a suck, did that mean you heard commands given to "bite" and to "suck"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether or not music was played during or after the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that music was played afterwards. It was afterwards that I heard music. When it was all over, one of those (and this was perhaps some 20, 25 metres away from me), I heard somebody call out "Two", he said, "I want two volunteers, strong men, we will do nothing to you, you will be all right", and I guess they went out. I do not know who went out. Nobody went out from my room. But when that was all over, then the music was played and the guard came and opened the door, and he said, "Now it is all right, it is all over and they have been taken to the hospital".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, during this approximate hour period that you heard the screaming and the crying, was it during that time that you heard two volunteers or two strong men being called for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, do you see Dule Tadic in court today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point him out and tell us what he is wearing, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The gentleman has a green jacket, an off-white shirt and multi-coloured tie.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect the identification of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. The record will reflect that the witness has identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination? Cross-examined by MR. KAY

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. Besic, from what you have told the Court this morning, you were not a particular friend of Dusko Tadic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not that I was not a particular friend of his. We were not very close friends, but we never met in the street without greeting each other, but we were not business partners. I did not turn to him for some business and neither did he to me, but if I would be alone in a coffee bar and if Dule would turn up, he would sit at my table and the other way around; if I found him in a coffee bar, then I would sit at his table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you told us that you may have been at a table with him in a coffee bar once a year or not even once a year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what you told us this morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it does not seem that you spoke to him particularly very often during the course of a year, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, over the last seven or eight years, probably less, but once before that we used often to swim together, to take -- I used to take a swim together in a pool that we had there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was that a long time ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, some six or seven years ago. Let's strike out the wartime, so let us not count that, that is, so it would be five or six years prior to 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what you say, you did not associate with his friends, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From time to time, yes. I had my company and he had his own friends. I socialised with his elder brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By his elder brother, do you mean an older brother or his eldest brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean elder brother, Ljubo. That is the one senior to Dule. Ljubomir is his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I would like to deal with now is where you were in this room, the electrical workshop, in the hangar building. It seems from what you indicated on the model that you were in the left-hand corner as you came in through the door of that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were against the wall that was furthest from the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you indicate to us that the corner where the wall at the back of the room is to be found -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I showed that I was not in that direction. I was on the left side by the wall in the corner. I was about one metre away from it, if one measures from the upper side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were one metre away from the back wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, towards the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anyone else who sat behind you in that spare space of one metre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One or two perhaps. I cannot say whether one or two, but I was not on the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you sitting on the floor or on a bench?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in between that position where you were and the door, there were a large number of people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all of them sitting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is not a room where the wall on that side goes straight down to the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes -- no, no, not straight. There is a corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that corner there had been a table, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was in that place that Jasko Hrnic used to sit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jasko Hrnic, at that moment Jasko Hrnic was sitting under the table or, rather, right in front of the table. He spent a lot of time on the table because he was often beaten and on the table he could stretch. He felt more comfortable on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he was under the table, did someone else or a number of other people then sit on top of the table?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it depended on the time, on the situation, who would then jump up on the table, to that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The door to this room was on that side of the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recollect whether the door opened outwards or inwards into the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It opens outwards if you look from out the room. If you are entering the room, then you open the door towards you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember which side of the door the hinges were? Were they on the wall side or the side of the -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you enter from the large room into the small room, into the electrical workshop, then the handle was on the right-hand side and there was the frame on the other side, on the left side, and with hinges. Of course, it was the other way around as you went out of the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the handle was on the side where the wall was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The hinges then were on the side where the wall was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We are sorry, we could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sir, if you could get closer to the microphone, the translation department -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course I can, sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The hinge then, was that on the wall side of the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recollect about how many people were in this room on this day that the names were called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 200.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your recollection is that the first name to be called was Eno Alic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not claim that Eno Alic was the first one to be called out. I only know that Jasko Hrnic was the last one to be called out and that he went out last.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jasko Hrnic left from your room, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All you can remember is that he was the last man to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other two, Eno Alic and Emir Karabasic, where were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In other rooms which I do not know, but I do know that beatings and the noise began when they came out. So this one was called out five or six times and he would not come out because of what normally happened when a man would be called out. So, he would not come out when he was called out. Then when Dule Tadic said, "Come out, I know that you are there. I'll kill you all" and then a commotion began among the detainees, and people began to say, "Jasko, go out because he is going to kill us".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the door to this room was closed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was only opened when Jasko Hrnic left the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The door was only opened to allow him out of that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but the conditions were not normal. One could not go out regularly, out of that room. As, for instance, here in this courtroom, it takes time to get out of the room, every step at a time, and Jasko had to, from a distance Jasko had to step over people, then open the door and then there was still time while as he crossed over the threshold, because there were too many people around. You could not approach the door normally. You had to feel it, you could not put your whole foot down or else you would tread on somebody's foot or head or hand or such like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are saying that at that door you saw Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when the door opened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not see any other guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say it is Dusko Tadic who was doing the talking to Jasko Hrnic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your position is right down there at the end of the room sitting down on the ground ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- looking over those bodies between you and the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was a door that was only open for a short period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, 10 seconds or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have made up this story that you saw Dusko Tadic at the door, Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true, and I have sworn that I will speak the truth. Sir, I am sorry. You are paid to do your job and I am doing because of ethical considerations, because I have a moral obligation to my people and my state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a relative of Jasko Hrnic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, his wife was a relative of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jasko was your cousin's husband, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The daughter, the uncle's daughter -- brother's brother's daughter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was a man you were very closely acquainted with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew him very well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Relatively.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Jasko Hrnic stood up to leave that room and walk through the people, you had to look through him because he was going towards the door, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I am ready to attend a reconstruction of these events on the site, if somebody guarantees my life and my security, and I can explain how it happened. I can do it also on this model here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are not a big man, Mr. Besic, are you? You are below average height? What sort of height are you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jasko Hrnic, was he a big man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure. He was, I guess, your height.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of large build?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not really, not very largely built, but he was tall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He looked a big and strong man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not look strong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Court has the photograph there and yes ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. (To the witness): This room, the electrical workshop, on this occasion was not a room where any of the guards or anyone else during this incident stepped into that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. They did not reveal themselves in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They appeared to be concealing themselves from you in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were hiding everything. They were hiding everything and lying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you could see clearly the figure the other side of the door as being Dusko Tadic, that simply is not true, Mr. Besic, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you not recognise a man if you knew him when he was 12, 18, 20, 25, 30, 35 or 40? Someone, I mean, just a glimpse suffices from 10 or perhaps 12 metres. It suffices to recognise him. Do you have to stare at a man whom you have known for 30, 40 years?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are telling us you recognised him because you heard stories about this incident ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- after it happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there not a lot of discussion in Omarska after this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What a discussion? Nobody talked about this event the whole night. Half of the people were simply silent about this event. Nobody dared speak out about the incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked about it with others in those days in Omarska before you left that camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there were some comments amongst ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next camp you were in, Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again you talked about this incident with others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure, yes, not only about that incident, about things that were going on, because in Manjaca we were safer. The Red Cross came to visit us every day. We were not ill-treated there. So that we rest a little bit and we could chat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked to a man called G. Do you know who I mean by G when I use that initial in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, do not mention his name, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I guess so, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You know you talked about this incident to him in Manjaca, that is right, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He and others had said to you it was Dusko Tadic who was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not told that. You asked me, did you see anything, and could I not see anything because I could not. It was simply in front of the mass of people. Had we gone into any detail, we, no, that is not true. Let me tell you, the man I talked to has very limited communication ability.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You picked up this story from others that it was Dusko Tadic who was there. That is why you have been prepared to come along and say of this single sighting of him in Omarska that he was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already told you that I had not made up this story, that it was an honour for me to be here, and you are here to invent and orchestrate things and I was there on the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To try to say that you knew his voice when you had hardly spoken to him in the previous period is a way to try to improve your identification of the guard at the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am telling you that I can recognise him again by his voice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you are saying to us, and this is your evidence, that the calling out and the taking of that man from the room was not by any other guard, it was by Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger? Re-examined by MR. TIEGER

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Besic, in the four or five years before the outbreak of the conflict, did you spend a lot of your time in central Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and I spent the last two years before the war, about two, two-and-a-half years before the war, in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you essentially there every day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every day, every day in the very centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Dule Tadic regularly in central Kozarac during that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when he would pass by. He was building his coffee bar then, so he often went through the centre of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, from the position you were sitting in, were other prisoners blocking your view of the face of Dusko Tadic in the doorway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I mean, one is standing, another one is sitting at a distance of seven or eight metres, and a man who is sitting down cannot conceal, cannot obstruct, the view of a person who is standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, do you know exactly in seconds how long that door was open?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already said about 10 seconds or so. It might have remained opened after that but, as far as I remember, it was not open afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As Jasko Hrnic left the room, did he block a portion of the doorway at some point as he was leaving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can show it to you. Jasko Hrnic was moving towards the door, not directly. His left side, his left hand was closest to the door. So he did not block it. He had to pick out where he could find some room to move and he zig-zagged. He could not walk step after step after step. He had to choose so he was zig-zagging through the room, picking out some free space on the floor to step there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dule Tadic stand in the doorway and block the door as Jasko attempted to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As Jasko is coming out, Dule stepped backward, opened the door and Jasko was moving ahead, that is, making for the threshold, and then I saw Tadic make a step backward. Jasko comes out. This one curses his mother and we hear a blow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. That is all I have.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, any recross?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, thank you, your Honour. Examined by the Court

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Witness, I thought you told us that it was Hrnic who opened the door, made his way through the bodies and opened the door, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that until he had opened the door you could not see who was outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, let me put it this way, do you recall the size of A17, of the room that you were in, in metres, from the length, from the door to the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the door to the back wall, eight perhaps 10 metres -- I cannot be more exact -- or perhaps nine maybe. I really, I really cannot say exactly. Eight times five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sure it is available to us in some other form. It is not clear to me exactly where you were sitting. I did not get the best view. Can you point out for me one more time where you were sitting, please? You tell me so I can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can, I can. I can show it, or do you want me to tell you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me -- show me, if you can, on that model and let us see if we can get a view.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: OK. I was here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait a minute. OK. How far?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me see. We have a floor plan here and it is not exact necessarily, but if it is A17 -- would you say that it was approximately a fourth of the distance from the back wall to where we have heard from other testimony a table was as the wall made an L shape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean from here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How far I was from there? Two-fourths or two-thirds towards the back wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two-thirds towards the back wall. So you were two-thirds away from the door, is that what you are telling me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the door, I am talking about the corner, I was about six or seven metres away from the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. So that corner you are referring to, you were about two-thirds back from that towards the back wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: OK. All we need is a measurement from the corner and we will understand that. Thank you. You may be seated. You indicated in a response to a question from Mr. Kay that you had spoken with witness G about this incident, is that correct, in Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes -- no, not me personally. We happen upon each other, we could walk, talk about it, not only about that, but about all the events because then we had much more opportunity there and more freedom of movement in Manjaca, within that enclosure which was called the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he talk with you about the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he talked about some unofficial things, things that one is reluctant to talk about or reluctant to even remember, but his abilities are very limited. He often swore when people would ask him about it and he was very reluctant to talk about the things he had gone through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I may follow that up when we return from recess? We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (11.30 a.m.) (The Court adjourned for a short time) (11.50 a.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Additional questions by Mr. Tieger or Mr. Kay? Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I may, your Honour? Further examined by MR. TIEGER

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, I may have asked a question earlier that was not clear. If I may, let me ask you about a few details of what you saw as Jasko Hrnic was leaving the room. First of all, is it correct that as Jasko Hrnic was leaving the room he was moving slowly and awkwardly because he was moving through a number of people in the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time before he got to the door, was the door open or closed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He reached for the door from a distance because he is tall, so he reached out, and that way he had the stability too, because he was moving zig-zag and he had to be careful where he was stepping.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After he opened the door, was he able to walk right through it or did he have to step around or by a prisoner or prisoners to get out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right, he opened the door before he got to the door. He just reached out. The door was open while he made additional steps so that he could reach the door.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is what I do not understand. Did Mr. Hrnic open the door or did someone else open the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Hrnic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As Jasko Hrnic moved to go through the door, through the doorway, did Dule Tadic step back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, when the door was open Dule Tadic was standing in front of the door and Jasko was still inside. He had not come out. He needed one more step to reach the threshold.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point as Jasko moved through the doorway did Dule Tadic step back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point after that, the door was again closed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was at some point during that process that you were seeing Dule Tadic, during that entire -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the previous process I saw Dule Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour -- no, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No one has any questions. Is there any objection to Mr. Besic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, you are permanently excused. You may leave. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness is Husein Hodzic. MR. HUSEIN HODZIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: When we resume this afternoon, we will resume in closed session and we will probably be in closed session for maybe 10 or 15 minutes to discuss matters that we discussed yesterday. So when we return from our lunch break, we will be in closed for 10 or 15 minutes to discuss those matters. Then we will go into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, would you please take that oath that is being given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Examined by MR. TIEGER

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Sir, what is your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hodzic, Husein.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what year were you born?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the town of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what part of Kozarac did you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A part that was called the old town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that very close to the central street of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was in the immediate vicinity of the main street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to school in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, elementary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you completed your education, did you serve in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what year did you serve and where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1985, in Montenegro, in Danilovgrad near Titograd.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then return to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a mining technician.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many mines are located in the area of Kozarac or Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is a system of mines, that is, the ore Ljubija and that was Omarska, Ljubija and Tomasica iron ore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those are operated by the same company or organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the same company, the same organisation. It is the mines of the iron ore Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which of the mines did you work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked both in Omarska and in Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which mine did you last work before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the iron ore mine of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately, when did you stop working at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seven to 10 days before the very attack on Kozarac, before the outbreak of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you working on the last day that you were present at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day there was no production, it did not exist. We just sat in the room of our administration. We were foremen and it was the so-called white house. That was the room where there would be the miners and us, the foremen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anything unusual happen on that date at the mine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes -- and it surprised me -- there was, arms were distributed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the arms distributed to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly to people of Serbian, in fact, all men of Serb ethnic national background.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, do you see the model in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that as showing a portion of the Omarska mine facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the administration building and the restaurant and workshop for repair of machinery. Behind is the white house which was where the roll call was being made for the miners and for us, and then to the left the small red building is what we called the wash house, where the equipment was to be washed after the shift whether from mud, from earth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the big concrete area on which those buildings are sitting used in the course of the production efforts or maintenance efforts at the mining facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was a parking lot, well, dumper truck and other equipment and trucks after the end of a shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The white house that you refer to, in addition to the roll calls which took place there for miners, were there offices there that were used by supervisors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that where your office was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The window to the right. The first room as you walked in, that was my office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, do you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since my 10th year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was it that you happened to know him as a child?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since Dusko Tadic was an athlete, he was a karate master and all children of Kozarac, including myself, were looking at him as a great man, an athlete, and maybe subconsciously we also wanted to do that sport. So that from an early age I knew him very well. For those reasons and in addition he also lived in Kozarac where I lived, so that I knew him well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you grew up, were your relations with him friendly up to the time of the tensions preceding the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the two of you, for example, greet each over when you met on the street or in cafes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. For the most part, yes, when we would encounter each other, maybe not shake hands every time, but we would greet each, which was with us "Hello".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know his parents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know his brothers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know his wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Her occupation, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the wife?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was a nurse in the dispensary in a health centre in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you also about a few other people from the area. Did you know Emir Karabasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was an active policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Jasko Hrnic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a well-known or popular person in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He had a transportation company. He also rode motor cycles. He was quite well known in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am just curious, do you happen to remember the colour of the motor cycle he had just before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Red and black. I am not exactly sure, but his cousin was killed on that motor cycle, so then after that he stopped riding it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Enver Alic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you related to Enver Alic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was your uncle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the three persons I mentioned, Emir Karabasic, Jasko Hrnic and Enver Alic good friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These three people were all Muslims, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dule Tadic know these three people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he knew them excellently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At different times were you together with one or the other of these people and Dule Tadic at the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have this photograph tendered as Exhibit 269 for identification, please? Mr. Hodzic, do you recognise the persons shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on this photograph are Emir Karabasic and Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this photograph as Exhibit 269 for admission, and ask that it be placed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 269 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Using the pointer, Mr. Hodzic, can you just point to Emir Karabasic? I am sorry, did you hear the question?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sorry, thank you. Mr. Hodzic with the pointer can you show us Emir Karabasic and Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the photograph).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. For the record, your Honour, the witness pointed to the man on the right as Emir Karabasic and the man on the left as Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, first of all, during the period of time after the elections of 1990 and before the outbreak of conflict, were there increasing tensions between Muslims and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
