utterances.text: I did not quite understand the question regarding tension. Yes, there was. After the elections, already there were signs of tensions between Muslims and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the outbreak of the conflict, did you notice whether there was any change in Dule Tadic's relationship with many of his Muslim acquaintances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one could notice that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he begin to associate primarily with one ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at that time for the most part almost exclusively he associated with people of Serb nationality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see who was frequenting his cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Members of the so-called Yugoslav People's Army, but at that time they were not members of that army because they wore different insignia with military, in military vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see persons of that army frequenting the cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As they come, arrived, parking on the pavement in front of his cafe and then walk inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what sorts of vehicles did they arrive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These vehicles were Pitzgauers from different company owners, but not with the insignia of JNA, of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of insignias did you see on those vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbian insignia, with four Cyrillic Ss or the Serb tri-colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, I noticed that you referred to the Pitzgauers. I do not know if that has been explained in court before, but perhaps you can tell us what a Pitzgauer is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a military vehicle. It is a field vehicle which can go off roads, village roads, then high inclines if there is snow on the road. In the back of the vehicle you can fit up to 10 people, up to about 10, which means something, six to 10 people. In front there is only one seat for the driver and another one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. One more point of clarification, is this a vehicle with wheels or with tracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With wheels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it an armoured vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not Dusko Tadic left Kozarac shortly or immediately before the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He left Kozarac on the eve of the attack on Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all Serbs in Kozarac leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some of them in the shelters with Muslims while the attack was taking place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you at home when the attack began on May 24th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you spend that day and the next day at home in your cellar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From time to time did you come out of the cellar to see what the situation was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when there would be a lull, a pause from all that shelling, then people would come out into the streets to register each other and to figure out how long it was going to last. We were looking for answers from each other, what we should do and such, and that was occasionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to the area of Brdjani at one point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The next day, on Monday, there was a large influx of people, of convoys, from Trnopolje, from Sivci, Menkovic on tractors, on horse carriages and on foot, and then we panicked and we all were looking for some rescue and there was a forest. We all wanted to hide there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there large groups of people trying to escape into the forest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Huge numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Tuesday, May 26th, did you surrender to Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About what time did you begin to do that? Did you leave your home for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the morning, late morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you join a group or column of surrendering people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that column going?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That column went in the direction of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did this group of surrendering Muslims indicate that it was surrendering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up front in the column there was a white flag and that was a sign that we were surrendering peacefully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the column proceeded in the direction of Prijedor, where did it stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The column stopped in Susici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any particular point in Susici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a bus stop and it was popularly known as "Limenka" which means that it was made from metal sheets -- "lim" means tin -- and people were waiting there. It was like a shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there Serb forces waiting there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had different uniforms on, different combinations, plus civilian clothes. Even I remember one especially, he had a bandana and it said "UN" on it. It looked like anything but the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there ways other than the way these people were dressed that made it appear different from the Yugoslav Army which you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was the insignia, there was a white eagle and then the Kokarda, the four Cyrillic Ss, and then that insignia "UN" is not the same as the Yugoslav People's Army which had a clear insignia with the five pointed star. A member of that army had to be well trimmed and shaven and not with long hair and a beard. I was a member of that Yugoslav People's Army in 1985.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the Serbian forces there at Limenka armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there military vehicles there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were military vehicles. There were armoured vehicles and personal weapons, infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any evidence of prior shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the road there were a large number of cases and casings from shells, I suppose that were used to shell in the previous two days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At Limenka, were Muslim men being separated from women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that happened first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What age limit was there for the designation of who would go with the men and who would stay with the children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 15, 16, even up to 70.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were you there with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was with my then six year old son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had your wife passed away three years earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While there were you confronted by a Serbian soldier who knew you and whom you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my colleague from work, Cedo Cunjak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Cedo Cunjak say to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He cursed my mother and said, "It is you I am waiting for".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attempt to reason with Cunjak or appeal to him in some way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I tried that, because he himself knew my situation, that I was an only parent, I had that child and I was in a situation to beg. In that moment he grabbed the child from me and he threw him on to the bus and before -- and the child cried and he said, "Don't worry, nothing will happen to you but something will happen to your father".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was Cunjak who said that to your son?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around that point did you see someone else you knew from before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw Goran Borovnica who lived in Kozarac who was a waiter in Kozarac, that is a Kozarac inhabitant, Goran Borovnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was Borovnica dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a camouflage uniform and a cap which covered his ears, unshaven, untidy, with a machine gun in his hands, in a hand, and another weapon -- an anti-tank weapon which he had over his shoulder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the years that you knew Borovnica, did you notice if there was anything unusual about his appearance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it was quite characteristic, because when he would look, his eyes were looking in different directions, one in one direction and one in the other one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Borovnica question you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he appear to be deciding what to do with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While Borovnica was talking to me his first question was where are my weapons, which I never had, and I told him that I had no weapons, that the only weapons in my house were the weapons of my father who was a hunter and he had a licence for it. He was standing there looking at me, and I realised that he was simply trying to figure out what to do with me, to liquidate me or to spare me. At moment he said: "Get on to the bus."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were on the bus were you spotted again by Cedo Cunjak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was curious. I wanted to see what was happening to other people arriving there. At that moment this Cedo Cunjak was passing by the bus on the side where I was sitting, looked up at my face very angrily, went round the bus, went on to the bus, and again indulged in his primitive checkpoint swearing and he took me off the bus again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he took you off the bus, did he express surprise that you were still alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. What happened first was, if I may quote him, "Fuck your mother, could you still be alive."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Cunjak hit you and then take you across the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there then a discussion between Cunjak and another Serb about both you and your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When Cunjak took me from the bus across the road Nedjo Kos, the driver of a bus for Autotransport where my brother Hikmet worked was standing there. Since we are somewhat similar he recognised me immediately, and asked Cedo, rather said to Cedo, "If he's like his brother, then they ought to be polished off right away." That clearly meant, to "polish off", it meant to liquidate us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they go with you in a search for your brother and eventually find your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Cedo Cunjak then ordered me to go from one bus to the other, look for my brother and get him off that bus. I could not but do it under the circumstances, but subconsciously I had made up my mind and I said I would not point at my brother. If I have to die, he does not have to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you passed in the vicinity of your brother did he make a gesture which brought attention to him and was recognised by them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that fraternal link, that love, he simply could not resist, but raised his head and asked: "What is it? What is it, Sendo?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your brother was located, the person for whom Kos and Cunjak that liquidated was intended, to whom were the two of you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Across the road, which means in the direction of Kozarac/Prijedor, to the left side of the paved road, the highway, Banja Luka/Prijedor, there was Goran Borovnica waiting for us again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Borovnica question you and your brother with more detail this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He asked my brother the same question as he had asked of me about the weapons, and my brother took out his licence for hunting weapons and for personal weapons and told him: "This is all I have and these are lawful weapons." Goran Borovnica took those two documents and he said, "I will check that when we make a breakthrough at Kozarac", and put them in his pocket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you and your brother put on the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, sir. At some point later on were you again taken off of the bus once more and threatened with liquidation, but finally managed to be on the bus when it began to move?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the bus stop in the area of Ziko's restaurant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Briefly, yes, briefly at the coffee which belonged to Ziko which we called Ziko's pub.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a gathering of Serbian forces there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How large and how well equipped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were super-well armed and there were very many of them, so any attempt to escape or anything was out of the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there also a large gathering of Muslim civilians there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a concentration of an enormous number of women, children, mixed with elderly. There was a large throng there. One could not even think of a figure, but I should say thousands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the area of Ziko's restaurant did the bus then transport you and the other men to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you held in Keraterm until the following night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day, the next evening we spent the night at Keraterm. Then the following day we spent the whole day at Keraterm and it was only that day in the evening, sometime in the late hours, we were again put on buses and transferred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you boarded those buses, where were you transferred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were transferred to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After arrival in Omarska, Mr. Hodzic, where were you first held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prior to interrogation I was in room 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you in room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seven or 10 days, around 10 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who interrogated me, yes, I was interrogated in the administrative building of my former company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the person who interrogated you before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Rade Kovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What nationality was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you beaten during the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the beating continue or last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Rade Kovic learn that you had formally been employed at the Omarska mine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When he asked me where I had worked I told him, here, in the Omarska mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say when he learned that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He then became even more hateful than before, so he swore, continued with beating, "You Muslims working in Omarska in the Serb mine and Serbs are at the employment bureau."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How badly were you beaten during the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So badly and so heavily that I still bear the effects of it. At that moment he either broke my jaw, dislocated it, I could not check that in Omarska to make an X-ray, but I still can hear my jaw, how disagreeably it functions, as if something were broken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the interrogation where were you held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was transferred to a room which we called "large room".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were both those rooms located in the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the ground floor or the first floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I ask either Miss Sutherland or the usher -- I would be happy to do it myself, if the Court would permit me -- to put the first floor back on the model so the witness can indicate where his rooms were?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hodzic, I am going to ask you in just a moment to leave your chair and indicate to us the rooms which you have mentioned. I will ask you to bring that pointer on the table in front of you and, in addition, put on the headphones which are located on the table across from you. If you have occasion to respond to a question if you could speak into the microphone to locate it at the same table that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you then to get up and point out first where room 15 was? Sir, if you could stand a bit to one side or the other so the Judges -- I think moving back is helpful, so you do not block the Judges' view. If you could show us again where room 15 was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, can you read the numbers which are written on the floor of the area which was room 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: B23 and B8, they are the wash basins and the lavatory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, sir, it appears the number may have been omitted. If you could recite those numbers quickly once again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: B7 is room 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us where the big room where you were moved after the interrogation was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What number or numbers are written on the floor of that room?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now looking back at room 15, there appears to be a door on the right side as you are now looking at the model. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking to the right side of that, is there another door on the other side of that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that door kept open or was it locked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was closed. It was locked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, prisoners from room 15 did not have access to the other portion of the first floor on the other side of that door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they could not pass through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the big room that you indicated, were there guards posted by the doorway on the first floor into that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did prisoners get into that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The prisoners used the staircase which led to this large room on the inside of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were guards posted on the ground floor ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking back at the area of room 15, there are a series of smaller doors, smaller areas passed room 15. What were those -- can you point those areas out first?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the area where there were concrete troughs with water taps where workers could wash their hands, wash off after a shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving left down the building beyond room 15 -- I am sorry, let me ask you this quickly. What is the area you just pointed to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the area where shower booths, where the workers also after a shift could take a shower, and they were shower booths.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking further left beyond room 15, there is a corridor and then there are rooms off that corridor, what were those rooms used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were smaller rooms, something like offices which, before the war, were used for various activities of the mine. One of those rooms when it became a camp was used by guards, guarding us in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you continue down the corridor to the left, is there a large room at the end, the room you are now indicating, what was that room used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This room here before the war was the design room for various drawings, a draughts room that we used in the mine for design projects.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time Omarska was operated as a camp, was that room also used to hold prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, at that time there were detainees in that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, looking back once again to the area of the big room, there are also rooms which appear to the left of that room. Can you indicate those? To your left in the area down the corridor as you are looking toward room 15, what were those rooms used for, the ones you are now indicating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were offices also. I do not really -- I did not know who they belonged to, but they are used as office premises of the mine and such like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the operation of the Omarska as a camp for Muslim and Croat prisoners, what were those rooms used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These two narrow rooms, they were the toilets, the two narrow ones, and the others, even though we were not allowed to use them, but we forced them open without a key and we would enter sometimes that room when it would be overcrowded. It was always be crowded, but some people used those rooms. I myself did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You can take your seat again. Mr. Hodzic, can you describe the general conditions in Omarska during the time you were held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The living conditions in Omarska from that first basic fundamental condition, drinking water, water that we used to drink, there was no drinking water at all because I used to work myself in that mine and we had never used it before. Those were industrial, it was industrial water used to wash machinery, the pista and nothing else. During our stay at the camp we drank that water and were happy when we had this undrinkable water to drink because even that was in short supply.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many toilets were there available to workers before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war one shift had about 150 workers, 50 people, and it was planned for that number to have a regular number of WCs, of toilets. When it was a camp half of these WCs got blocked and we were thousands there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the result of -- let me ask you this. Even of the toilets that worked or even referring to the toilets that worked, were prisoners able to use those freely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the result of the absence of sufficient toilets and the fear of using even those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The consequence if I decided to use such a toilet, then it was considerable. One could expect to be beaten up, to be hit, to be battered. So many people simply chose not to and they used for the purpose boots, some plastic canisters, even trousers, and then they would wait for a moment. Sometimes there would be a decent guard who would allow us to go out quickly and throw it away. That is how we somehow managed, not easily, but we somehow managed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the beatings of prisoners who tried to use the toilet, were there beatings on the way to get food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was a daily occurrence and nothing new. We had simply got inured to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were prisoners called from their rooms and beaten or killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see bodies in Omarska, bodies of Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know with what kind of transport, vehicle those bodies were generally removed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In vehicles which belonged to the Omarska mine, TAM, a small TAM, a yellow one, a large FAP truck, but mostly the vehicles that belonged to the mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The TAM truck was a smaller truck, is that right, a smaller flat bed truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes smaller.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The FAP truck which you referred to is a large vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, not that large, but large enough. Its carrying capacity was about eight tonnes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see the FAP truck or a FAP truck used to transport bodies from Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, once I saw that FAP truck, one could not load by hand the dead bodies, so that a loader was brought up with a huge ladle, loading ladle, and they then shoved those bodies there, so that this loading ladle would lift them all and then throw them into the truck. I mean, as they once used to load rock and stone, thus they did with those dead bodies. That truck would sometimes be full of these bodies. Some of them were already stiff, some were mutilated. They simply were bodies no longer. That was sheer horror.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that FAP truck shortly after a large group of new prisoners had arrived from Hambarine in July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw that truck then when a group of prisoners arrived from the area of Hambarine and neighbouring villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was after their arrival you saw the truck loading those dead bodies sometime after those prisoner had arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess until 2.30. As I indicated, when we return we will be in closed session for 10 to 15 minutes. (1.00 p.m.) (Luncheon Adjourned) (2.30 p.m.) (Closed Session)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (3.20 p.m.) (Short Adjournment) (3.30 p.m.) (Open session)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are going to continue straight through until 5.30 since we have been busy in closed session taking care of matters. The Court reporter will not mind that? Very good.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, are you going to call your next witness, or we have not finished with Mr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sorry, I do not have his name here. OK. Very good. Ask him to come in. MR. HUSEIN HODZIC, recalled. Examined by MR. TIEGER, continued.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be seated, sir. Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Hodzic, just a couple of quick matters about some things you discussed earlier. First you mentioned at one point that the water which had been previously used for industrial purposes, such as to wash the pista, was used in camp for drinking water by the prisoners. When you refer to washing the pista before the war, were you referring to the entire concrete area where the large machinery was parked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned when discussing Jasko Hrnic that he owned motor cycles. Then you mentioned that his brother was killed on one of them and he did not want to ride that one any more. Did Mr. Hrnic have other motor cycles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what kind or what colour they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were large motor cycles, Kawasaki and Suzuki. Mostly those motor cycles were just large and he changed them frequently. It was a hobby of his and, as a business man who had a private company, private transport company, could afford something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the colour of any of those motor cycles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember one of his Kawasaki motor cycles. It was 50 cubic centimetres and I had a pleasure to ride on it with him. On one occasion he was driving and I was sitting behind so I remember that the best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the colour of that particular one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That motor cycle was red.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Before you leave that, we are only concerned with the motor cycle that he last had, are we not? As I understand the witness, he is talking about all the motor cycles he has had over the years.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Maybe that was not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Would you make that clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, your Honour. Because you are right, I started off by addressing the motor cycles which he still had after the other one was wrecked. (To the witness): Mr. Hodzic, the motor cycle you just referred to, the red one you had ridden, did Mr. Hrnic still have that immediately before the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he still did, I think that was the one he had at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hodzic, getting back to Omarska, were prisoners regularly called from their rooms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did some of those prisoners return?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the condition often of those who did return?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They looked like they were beaten up, some could come on their own power, some were brought in in a blanket, in different situations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember a man named Silvio Saric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he Chairman of the HDZ party in Prijedor before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he called from the room and returned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was called out, and he did return.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His condition was one of the worst of all the men that were going and coming back. He was -- he had to be brought back. He could not walk on his own power. He only showed signs of life in that he was breathing heavily and he was looking. All the other functions of his body were non-existent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Saric die from his injuries some days after he was returned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He died in that room after several days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some prisoners called from their room and killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know, for example, a man named Sefik Sivac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he do before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war he had one of the more luxurious restaurants in Kozarac called "De Luxe" and then he changed the name into "International" and then he had a coffee bar in Prijedor at the old market.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, had he been beaten before he was called out of the room for the last time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Sefik Sivac was called out of the room for the last time, did you later see his body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the next day I saw his body, dead body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the condition of his body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It looked like anything but a body. The clothes were torn up. There were clear signs of blood. It was simply -- it was a terrible shape the body was in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was his body alone or was it in a pile of bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His body was on a pile of bodies, somewhere around 10, eight or 10, bodies. I recognised his body and another body of another man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for the record, I noticed that it said twice on the transcript "Dzavid Sivac", and the name I asked about was Sefik Sivac, is that correct? You were speaking about Sefik Sivac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sefik Sivac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some prisoners called from the room and simply disappeared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, did you have a particular place where you normally stayed in the big room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we all had certain places. Once you enter, the first time you entered, whoever found a place they tended to stay there. We got used to that. I had my own place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Emir Karabasic in your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was his place close to yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was the third man away from me, from the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to leave your chair and point out to us where your place was in the room and where Mr. Karabasic's place was on the model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (The witness indicated on the model) This was my place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, would that be, as you enter, by the rear wall near the left corner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my head was against a wall which means that I was the last in that row against the wall, here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Emir Karabasic was close by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the left, the third person from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the Court able to see that last shot?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Not the last shot. I did not see the very last shot, but I saw him when he first pointed to where he located where he was sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There was just a better angle on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Show it again. Let us see.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If you could again show us where your spot was? If you could just very quickly again show us where your spot was, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am sorry. Could you return to your seat -- before you do, let me ask you a couple of other questions. Do you know where Enver Alic was, where he was held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Enver Alic was in this room, but in the hallway, here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Jasko Hrnic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the room below the large room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you may be seated. Was it sometimes possible for prisoners in one room to visit prisoners in another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did that depend on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It depended on the guards, from the individual guard, from the person, to what degree he was forthcoming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that Emir Karabasic and Jasko Hrnic were good friends. Did Emir Karabasic sometimes visit Jasko Hrnic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the day when Emir Karabasic was called out of that big room for the last time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the approximate date that occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not the date, but it happened in June, between 15th and 20th June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the approximate time of day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the afternoon, between 4.00 and 6.00. I do not know the exact time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had Emir Karabasic been called out before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his condition on the day he was called out the last time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in a very bad condition, with very marked signs of beatings. He was all black. You could clearly see the marks from the chain which were on his chest, from some iron bars, because there was a straight line. About 90 per cent of his body was black, even his soles because he was bare foot, no socks, so his soles were black which was a great problem for him because he was not able to walk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he recovering from those previous beatings on the date he was called out for the last time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. He pretty much recovered. I do not know if he was fully recovered, but almost.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had Emir Karabasic expressed concern about the possibility of anyone coming to camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, his greatest worry was if Dule Tadic came. I think that he feared that the most, and he was repeating that and he was insisting on that. I did not know why. I tried sometimes when I had an opportunity to ask him why him. I thought that he was a friend of his, a long time friend; perhaps even he could expect some help from him and not fear because Emir and I were good friends. On one occasion he managed to tell me only that, "I saw something that I was not supposed to see, I was somewhere where I should not have been". He did not say what he saw and where he was, but he was very frightened. He was so full of fear from the very thought of Dusko Tadic. I did not understand -- perhaps even today I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I raise a matter here? We are plainly in an area involving prejudicial evidence that, in my submission, prevents the defendant from having a fair trial, because of the nature of this evidence that is reported conversation from a third party and would fall within that category of hearsay about which the Defence has previously made submissions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, even in a jurisdiction which has rigid hearsay rules, this evidence would fall within the state of mind exception. In addition, it is a predicate to a further statement that was made in contemplation of death.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May I reply to that? First of all, there is no ground of settled helpless expectation of death which is the exception to the hearsay rule the number of jurisdictions acknowledge to enable hearsay to be included. There is nothing within the material adduced by the Prosecution that show that at the time of any statements being made by this party, that they fell within that particular category. The state of mind of the party that is being referred to is not relevant to the issue here. I cannot see how it is relevant in relation to acts done by another that the state of mind of a third party has any bearing upon the matter at all. If the Prosecution are approaching these matters on that basis, my submission is that there is a fundamental flaw in the way that they are presenting this evidence and the basis of their argument.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, your Honour, I think it is clear that the state of mind of this particular victim plays a role in the overall analysis of this incident in this case and is probative when placed within the context of the overall facts. Second, this particular statement was not elicited -- I am not basing this particular piece of evidence on the contemplation of death at that particular moment, but this is a predicate to a statement that was made when this victim was confronted by the very possibility he feared and at that moment, if I am allowed to elicit the evidence, he clearly believed that he was a dead man. That statement has all the reliability in addition, as you will hear, to being present sense impression and a spontaneous utterance that would permit its admission, even in a strict hearsay jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As we have repeatedly said, our 10 Rules of Procedure and Evidence in no way specifically exclude hearsay. We have 89(C) that provides for the admission of testimony that is relevant and has probative value. The motion that you have filed regarding hearsay, which we have promised to give you a decision this week on -- we heard argument last week, we are working on it now -- there are really two parts to that motion. One, that any evidence that is offered that directly implicates the guilt of the accused be excluded if it is hearsay and does not, I gather, fall within one of the traditional exceptions in your written papers. You cited two, excited utterances and another one I forget. The second part, though, of your motion is that the Judges not hear any such testimony, even if it fits within the exception, until we determine the circumstances under which that testimony was received. We have not ruled, but we obviously are working on the decision and discussing it. Consistent with that, I will overrule your objection. Our focus again is probative value. 89(D) allows the Tribunal or allows this Trial Chamber to exclude any evidence which, although it has probative value, is substantially outweighed by the need to provide a fair trial. It does not say "prejudicial effect", "fair trial". At this point, we are looking at that particular Rule as allowing us to hear this testimony. It is certainly relevant. It appears to have probative value. If it appears that it is substantially outweighed by the need to provide Mr. Tadic with a fair trial, then we will exclude it from consideration. It will not play a role in our reaching a decision in this matter. So I will overrule your objection. Mr. Tieger, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Listening to Mr. Tieger raise these objections and both of you argue about the technicalities, it just elucidates the problem that is faced in an International Tribunal where we are all working together in a new system that combines civil systems, where hearsay is not even a factor, and then common law systems. Mr. Tieger, from the United States, is referring to all of these exceptions that I may be familiar with; you are referring to these exceptions that Judge Stephen and Judge Vohrah may be familiar with. We are focusing on an entirely different matter and that is the probative value of the evidence. When we give you our decision, we hope that you understand our analysis but I will overrule your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Did Emir Karabasic say to you what he thought would happen if Dule Tadic did come to camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was very clear. He said he would be no more, which meant that he would be killed. I am quite clear about that. It was not only once, it was on several occasions that he said something to this effect, "If Dule comes, then I am gone, I am finished".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did he look when he said those things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He looked as I have never known him before -- frightened out of his wits, poor, fearful. A man who had never been frightened by anything before, who was a man very conscious of his dignity, and he had fallen so low.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that when you enquired he would not tell you exactly why he was afraid. Were prisoners reluctant to talk to each other about things they had seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was, one might say, the first and basic thing to tell someone because the more you knew the greater the chances were of being killed. So that people, brother concealed from his brother, because if he knew something, then you would be killed so that you would not know it any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, just to clarify a translation. This translation says: "Yes, it was, one might say, the first and basic thing to tell someone because the more you knew the greater the chances were of being killed". Was that to tell new prisoners that they should not talk to one another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what we felt, because if someone saw an act, a monstrous act, which had taken place, shortly after that he would also disappear, but not all, fortunately not all, not all of us. Some people survived because it is impossible to destroy a people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the day or the afternoon that Emir Karabasic was called out for the last time, how was he called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Emir Karabasic is to go down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the voice come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the ground floor, from the room in front of the entrance door through which one had to go through in order to climb up to that large room in which I and Emir Karabasic were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did Emir Karabasic react? How did he look after his name was called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He jumped up, pale, frightened. He stood up in order to cross to the window. He had to step over my foot, over my legs. So he got to the window, bent, inclined and then he turned to us, he was also facing me at that moment, and at that moment I thought that he would out of fear die, but all he uttered was, "Dule has arrived, I am finished".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have this photograph marked as Exhibit 270 for identification, please? Can that be called up on the screen as 15/32? Mr. Hodzic, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the room in which I was, in which Emir Karabasic was also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The wall shown on the right side of the picture, is that the rear wall of the room against which you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the back wall by these blue lockers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the blue cabinet there at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the window shown somewhat to the right of centre of the photograph, the window to which Emir Karabasic went after his name was called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he do when he got to that window?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That window was the source of oxygen, of air, to us, and it was always open, and he went across the window. He did not have to lean across that window because the view was quite clear. Then he turned and said that, "Dule has come, I am done with".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did he look at that moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So scared, so without a single trace of optimism that he might ever come back after that call out. No optimism and a great deal of fear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Emir Karabasic go downstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What could you hear happening on the ground floor of the hangar after he went downstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What could you hear from the ground floor of the hangar after Emir Karabasic went downstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A beating, battery began immediately, obscenities. That monstrous act was already taking place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear other prisoners called out after Emir Karabasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard about Jasko Hrnic. He was called several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this. How long did the sounds of beating and the cries that you heard from downstairs continue for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can judge, since we had no watches, nor would it occur to anyone to look at the time, but it must have lasted about one hour, perhaps 10 minutes less or 10 minutes more, but we had no watches. They had been taken away from us by those guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell how many prisoners were being beaten from the sounds that were coming from downstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several of them. I could recognise some of them by their voices because those screams were alternating, not from the same man. It is different. It is, you knew a man, you know a man very well and then he screams or wails, and then it continues with the second one, with a third one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to tell how many guards or other people were involved in beating the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were a number of guards, a number of them. I do not know how many. I could not count them, but there were a number of them because one man cannot perform all these blows so quickly and to reach all of them, and they all had their curses. One could clearly distinguish, clearly realise, there were several persons. How many, I could not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the hour or so this went on for, did you hear any orders being given?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, those were those orders which I could not believe a man with dignity could utter, "Bite", "Pull", "Grab", "Tear", to that effect. I know, clearly, that it referred to the genitals, because at a point I heard, if I may use very brutal language, "Bite off his balls" and that was quite clear what it meant because a man has them in only one place. That pain, the pain of those people, that painful scream, it was so awful. Hitchcock is nothing, a director, I mean, he is nothing to them, to show something like that. Through pain, through wails, they were imploring them, those people subjected to this were imploring them, but the perpetrators seemed to draw courage from that, and it would grow louder and louder and beatings became stronger. That was horrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As this was going on, did you try not to listen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did try that, to somehow plug my ears. I prayed to God not to be there because those cries of pain, it was difficult and for a normal man, it was very difficult for a normal man to endure them. So I tried to put my head down, to put my hands over my ears and then I had to do it again, come, maybe I will hear somebody surviving, and then I would again cover my ears. It was -- if I had to go through that once again, I do not think that I would survive, just barely listening to it. This is the worst, worst thing that ever happened to me in the camp and in my life. It is difficult, it is difficult to describe it. You can only have bad luck and experience it. Only if you really have bad luck, if you have no luck at all, can you experience something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, when the sounds from the ground floor of the hangar finally stopped, that is, the sounds which you have described, did you later hear anything else happening in the hangar? Did you hear what happened after the incident was over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they stopped the beating and those screams, those wails, I do not know whether to call them, then a lull ensued, a lull. I do not know how long it lasted. I do not know what dead silence is, but that is an expression repeated often. There was dead silence. Then we heard the sound of that small truck, of that TAM, and when that sound disappeared then one could hear washing, that something was being washed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not music was played during the incident or after the incident was over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then music was often the motivation and it also helped them. It boosted their morales, those guards, those men, I do not know what their names are. I do not want really to insult them, but those men, those humans, they were playing music. The music referred to a text which is imprinted on my mind, "Let me live, don't touch my happiness", and the translation of those lyrics is clear enough and shows what they intend to do when the tortured person was experiencing two kinds of pain, one for being beaten and the other one listening to a song which is provocative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, did you ever see Emir Karabasic, Jasko Hrnic or Enver Alic alive again after that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Dule Tadic in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then I was lining up for lunch, 30 of us in a group and, as I came out, there was already a column in the kitchen and we were waiting ready along the wall of this building in front of me. At the corner by the kitchen stood Dusko Tadic whom I know very well, and I felt fear creeping through me so as not to be spotted by him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that on the corner directly across from the position where the prisoners lined up? The corner of the kitchen directly across from the position where the prisoners lined up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and I was looking forward directly, that is, my eyes were turned in his direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were the prisoners lined up that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One behind the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Facing which direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The direction of the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your right shoulder would be against the wall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, towards the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the prisoners always line up in that way before going to lunch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not always. There were instances when we had to face the wall, sometimes to look down at our feet. It varied. More often than not, we were not allowed to look either forward or to any of the sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Dule Tadic wearing that day, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember he had a uniform, a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers or guards in the area where he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from my viewpoint to the left of him and it was the common picture, that is, that was where the guards stood every day. That was the sentry post. A guard would stand there and provide some cover from the sun. They improvised something, some kind of shade, and he was standing in front of them and by the very corner of the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you had seen and recognised Dule Tadic there and began to move forward to go to lunch, did you make an effort not to be seen by him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then I did what I could so as not to be spotted by him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not he was still out there when you returned from lunch a few minutes later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was still there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, do you see Dule Tadic in court today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do I see him?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, can you look around and tell us if you see Dule Tadic in court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see him. He is sitting between two policemen, rather sour faced with a tie. I can see him well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May the record reflect the identification of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The record will reflect the identification of the accused by the witness but, Mr. Hodzic, please refrain from any negative descriptions. Just describe what Mr. Tadic is wearing. That is sufficient. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I have nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Cross-examined by MR. KAY

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, from what you tell us then, you did not see Dule Tadic in the camp on this afternoon that Emir Karabasic was called out from that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did, I saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that you were told by Emir Karabasic that he had a fear of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that he confided that to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Emir Karabasic was a well-known man from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Many people in that camp knew who he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I guess so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What he appeared to be saying to you was, "If Dusko Tadic visits the camp and knows I am here, then something will happen to me"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what he told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was no indication from Emir Karabasic before that afternoon that Dusko Tadic had visited the camp and knew that he was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not tell me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that afternoon when Emir Karabasic was called out, can you recollect anyone else being called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Jasko Hrnic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Eno Alic, for instance, did you know that he was called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not called out, to my hearing. I did not hear it. How he went out of the room, I do not know, but he was not called out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anyone else being called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That afternoon?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, it is just those two names that you heard and you were in this room on the first floor at the end of the corridor when you heard those names being called, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the room that you had stayed in during your period of detention in Omarska until the end when you were moved from that camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but before the interrogation I was in room 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you stayed in this room until you were eventually moved elsewhere in August, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on that afternoon when these incidents took place, did you talk to other people about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that event?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have enough courage, because if one should start enquiring around us about something, then it could become dangerous for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who I mean when I identify a witness as G? Have you been told that this is a name by which someone who was in the camp should be described if he is mentioned in these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to look at this piece of paper here. I do not want the ladies and gentlemen in the public gallery to see it behind you, so make sure you look at it in front of your body, then fold the piece of paper up.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just put it flat on the table. Do you want to show that to the Prosecutor? (Handed). MR. KAY (To the witness): That name I wrote down on that piece of paper, is that someone whom you knew in Omarska as being involved that afternoon in what was happening in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that and I am not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that person whom we will call G, do you understand, that afternoon taking part in these events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That afternoon I could not see that event, and I could not see the person G.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because what I want to suggest to you is that you have told this court that Emir Karabasic mentioned Dule Tadic as he was leaving that room because you want to implicate Dusko Tadic in what happened there that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not want to blame Dusan Tadic. I want to see the one blamed who is guilty of something and not personally just Dusko Tadic. I would be happier to defend him rather to accuse him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I am suggesting to you is you have made that up to involve him in what you say you heard taking place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true. I did not make it up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you always spoken about what happened that afternoon without making up what you believe happened, without inventing part of the story?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not make anything up or add anything to the story and I would appeal to you, sir, to ask me shorter questions because it is difficult for me to answer after such a long question is asked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you always told the truth about what happened that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, from what you say, you never saw what happened in that hangar when those screams were being uttered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to look at this statement that you made and I will give it to you in your own language. It is a statement that was taken in the form of an interview. For identification purposes, your Honour, might it be called D24 which is the next number? I believe the Prosecution has have a copy of this already. I would like to put that statement before you. You will see it is something written in your own language. Do you remember giving a statement in July 1993, about a year later, on a questionnaire in relation to a body called Refugees from the Former Yugoslavia? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it. It was not a statement. It was a story how I survived the camp, and there was no distinction made between what I heard about and what I experienced, so it was just the whole story about the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was written down with an interpreter present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was an interpreter to whom I immediately had an objection because he was Albanian and his knowledge of the language that I speak was very poor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whatever his knowledge of the language was, you do not think that he would have started making up things that you had seen, do you, Mr. Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But things can be confused, what I heard and what I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could just turn to page 5 and you will see in the middle a heading at paragraph 6 called, "Incident, a murder on 16th June 1992 of four people who were close to me".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that? I would like you to take this opportunity to read through that page 5 and page 6 of this statement and the top parts of page 7 -- there is no need to read it out loud. You can read it to yourself and then I will ask some questions about it to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have finished reading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. If you would like to turn to page 6 of that statement, you can see the names mentioned there, you claim in this statement that one of the guards called out four names, Enver Alic, Emir Karabasic, Jasko Hrnic and Fikret Harambasic, is that right? You will see the names Enver Alic and Emir Karabasic on page 5.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is how it is stated here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you claimed that those four names were called out, but that is not something you actually heard, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard only two names being called out, and this statement of mine is a statement which is just a story about my being in the camp, what I heard and what I saw. This is -- there is no distinction here between what I heard and what I saw, like it is now in this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that right, because you will notice at the end of the sentence in that top paragraph on page 6, you say that most of what you are going to describe you witnessed with your own eyes, "Everything else I heard". Perhaps you would like to read out those last two sentences in that top paragraph on page 6 beginning, "Vecinu"? Perhaps you would like to read that out to the court out loud?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Most of what I am now going to describe I witnessed with my own eyes. Everything else I heard".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the next paragraph you describe that, "they were brutally beaten with rifle butts and iron bars in front of our hangar where we could see", is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "They were ordered to lie on the ground. They were beaten from all sides on all parts of their bodies".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, it says, "Where we could see them".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is plural, and then from that plural I could hear something because up there it says, "I heard the rest".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not see anyone being beaten in that hangar, as you told this court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That afternoon I did not see anybody being beaten. I only heard that beating going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yet in this statement you claimed to have seen it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That "we saw", that could also mean that somebody else who saw it could have told me about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To describe that they were beaten on all parts of their bodies is not something to do with hearing the incident, it is claiming to have seen it, because how would you know they were beaten on all parts of their bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was beaten up myself and I know that they beat you up on all parts of the body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that paragraph you go on to say, "It was the worst thing we saw"? That is right, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but in what paragraph?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that second paragraph on page 6, after you describe them being brutally beaten and it being in front "where we could see" and after they were beaten on all sides of their bodies, you say, "It was the worst thing we saw".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and again in this sentence as well it states what we saw, which means again it is several people who saw it, and I could have heard it from those people because this was only a story that the person to whom I was giving the interview had a picture of what happened to us in that camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also go on further in this statement to say, "15 minutes later the torturers fetched another Muslim out, G", and the letter G is used in this translation instead of his full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the next sentence to that, "The torturers opened the door to my hangar and took the first person they saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were claiming that G came from your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the person where G was staying belonged to our room. We shared the same door to enter and exit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "The torturers formed an alley. G had to take the virtually lifeless bodies by the ankles or the arms and drag them through the alley like a sack of potatoes. While he did so, the torturers beat the virtually lifeless bodies again. When he had dragged one person through, he had to drop the body and drag another person".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what you were claiming to have seen? You claimed to have seen things that afternoon that were not true, that you did not see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
