utterances.text: I did not see that and it is clear in each that it was a plural, that it was -- which is different from "I". "We" and "I" is different and that was a story of a camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But why are you mentioning here G when you knew nothing about G being involved in this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the conversations had become possible after this danger ceased, I did not want to remind him of things that were so difficult for him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we just look at that next paragraph: "The first time that Jasmin Hrnic was dragged through the alley he was already dead. I know it was Hrnic because one of the Serbs commented that as a motor cyclist he had not been so weak. I knew that Hrnic was the only motor cyclist".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does not say when he was dragged through the first time, but when Jasmin Hrnic was so dragged through the line-up, and it does not say first or second or third time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did not see that at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see that. I am not claiming to have seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why have you said it in this statement that is being caused to bring you here as a witness for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a number of objections to that question. I guess the primary one is counsel is rehashing the same point over and over through each paragraph and reasking the same question which the witness has answered many times. Secondly, with respect to that particular question, I do not think there is any basis for the Defence to build into their questions suppositions about the basis for calling any witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am sorry if it gives Mr. Tieger discomfort.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The witness has said several times that, "This is not a statement, but a story of what I heard as well as what I saw". So very often you ask him, "Why is this in the statement when you did not see this?" The answer has always been, "This is not a statement of what I saw. It is a statement, as I said in the beginning, of what I heard and saw". So I can overrule your objection. It is just he keeps saying over and over, and you are basically eliciting a lot of information regarding an occurrence this witness did not testify about today because he says he did not see it. If you want to continue reading about all of these things that he says other people heard and told him, you can do so. I will overrule the objection. MR. KAY (To the witness): Again when you made this statement you said that G was ordered to drink motor oil, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I gave this story about the camp, not the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this statement, though, you said, as we have looked at on the top of page 6, "Most of what I am now going to describe I witnessed with my own eyes. Everything else I heard".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whatever I heard or seen, I related to this honourable court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You on this occasion made a statement which was being prepared to enable the Prosecution of people believed to be Serbian war criminals, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to object. This examination started off when counsel himself asked the witness about what was entitled "The questionnaire for refugees from the Former Yugoslavia". It is an extremely unfair question he is now requesting.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The question is whether or not this was a statement that enabled the Prosecution to believe that Serbian war criminals -- I cannot read the rest of it. Unless this witness has some personal knowledge that somehow this statement was going to be given to the Prosecution, and then the Prosecution would then make an assessment of it to determine whether they would file an indictment, I think it is inappropriate. It calls for conclusions really that he is not able to make. This is up to the Prosecution. His statement, I gather, was not taken by the Prosecution. It was taken by who, The Refugees -- some organisation. I do not recall the full name of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Taken without conditions for the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Refugees from former Yugoslavia, yes. I will sustain the objection. It is speculative. It calls for a conclusion I think this witness cannot make. MR. KAY (To the witness): Let us see, Mr. Hodzic, if you can deal with this as you have had plenty of opportunity to rely on the fact that you were relating matters that you knew from the history of the camp. If you just look at that paragraph concerning G being ordered to drink motor oil, do you also say, "From this point on I could not keep watching"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What page is this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 6 in the middle. "We heard G being ordered to drink used motor oil".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Then I heard", not "seen", "how G was ordered and then from that moment I could not see things any more". So that is where the error in translation comes in because "heard" and "seen" is different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. "I could not see things any more" implies that you were saying you could see them before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I keep repeating -- I do not know how many times I need to repeat -- this statement, this story about our experience of the camp is not about accusation, a questionnaire to all the detainees, all the refugees from the former Yugoslavia to in some way provide a picture, an approximate picture, of what happened. There was nothing, there were no strictures given at that time what we needed to do precisely, so I just told a story.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to this matter you go on, as you have seen in your statement, to give lots of details about G and what he was supposed to have done that afternoon, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, when we "heard", I do not see that -- if you see anywhere that I say "I saw", "We then heard G being ordered to drink used motor oil", etc. Later, he said, he told me that he had to drink so he was telling me. My statement is about both seeing and hearing it from others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this statement you do not say that you heard Emir Karabasic say, "Dule is here, I am finished"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I was to tell everything that I saw and I heard, it would last a very long time. It would be more than one volume of a book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I suggest to you is this, that you heard a rumour that Dule Tadic was involved in this, is that right or wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did not G come up there to that large room and there be rumour amongst all of you about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The person G after that was almost speechless after that, because after that act that he was ordered to perform, it was difficult to talk about anything, let alone him coming and saying, "Hey, there was Dule Tadic around and this and that". I do not know if you realise what it means to be in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not know that there was a second volunteer out there in the hangar with G, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could not be one person. One person was not enough to meet their needs for entertainment, to drag, to pull, to do all this, to hold him. One person could not do that. It is only natural that there were more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I suggest to you is this, that because of that rumour and you claiming to have seen more to other people, that is why you have come here to implicate Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Your Honour, I have tendered the statement. May it be exhibited as D24? It was my omission to remember to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. What is the number?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It has been offered for identification purposes. You want it to put it in. Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is already part of the Court's materials as tendered by the Prosecution. In so far as the statement is concerned -- the translation of the document which is being tendered, that is not something that I am familiar with. We tendered to the Defence an English translation of the questionnaire. Now there is a Serbo-Croat translation which, I gather, is being tendered to the Court. I would at least like an opportunity to see the extent to which it conforms to the original versions. But, with that reservation, I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then we will reserve a ruling on it. Let us have an opportunity for them to review the English and make sure that it has been properly translated, at least according to the Prosecution's view of the translation. Perhaps there will be no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour will recollect the witness has been through it with me live, so I have no objection to 24A being the Serbo-Croat, B being the English.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think the point Mr. Tieger is -- have you read the entire statement? I am sorry, then I missed it. I thought just portions of it have been read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This incident is section 6. I summarised the end.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The English will be admitted as 24B.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 24A will be admitted, subject to the Prosecutor having an opportunity to confirm the translation that you have made of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is from the Tribunal, this is from the Registry. This is done for us.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: By the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, do you have a copy of 24A? That is the Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It will be admitted. If there is a problem in translation we will resolve it later. 24A and 24B will be admitted. Give the Prosecution a copy of 24A, please. Mr. Tieger, any redirect? Re-Examined by MR. TIEGER.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps just one question, Mr. Hodzic. If you can turn to the first page of that questionnaire, at the bottom of the first paragraph, the last sentence, did the translator or the interpreter to whom you were speaking and during the course of this questionnaire understand you to say that you tried to summarise some of the worst events of Omarska, and is that reflected in the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean whether the interpreter understood that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, is that what appears in the, at least does that appear in the copy of the questionnaire which you have in front of you at the bottom, just before incident one is recounted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "I experienced some terrible things during this period. I shall try to briefly refer to the worst incidents."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what you tried to do for the people who were questioning or asking you to complete this questionnaire process on that day, give them some understanding of what had happened in Omarska and what information you could provide about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I was trying to do, just to give them a rough picture of what was going on in this camp. I did not see it as a statement because I cannot base a statement on hearsay, of something more important. This was just a story. I was just telling a story about something that happened in my life while I was at a camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you sir. I have nothing further. Your Honour, Miss Sutherland reminds me that we did not tender Exhibit 270 for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That was the photo of Mr. Karabasic and Mr. Tadic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour that was the photo of the large room.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Of where the witness was. OK, very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No objection to Exhibit 270?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could have one more moment. I have nothing further. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have no questions. Sir, you are permanently excused -- is there any objection to this witness being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You are permanently excused. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at all. (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, you will call the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour the Prosecution will call Mr. Armin Mujcic. MR. ARMIN Mujcic, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please stand and take the oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Examined by MR. KEEGAN.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you state your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Armin Mujcic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your date of birth, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 26th April 1968.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you born in the town of Kozarac in the opstina of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you raised and where did you attend school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was raised in Kozarac and that is where I completed four grades of the elementary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was "Kozarusa" not" Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After completing the four years of school did you go on to school in Kozarac itself and then in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your occupation, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a locksmith.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you complete your compulsory military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what year was that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you trained as?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As a tank operator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a driver or a gunner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A gunner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you returned home to the Kozarac area did you serve any reserve duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the last time you performed reserve duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the eve of the war, at the outbreak of the war in Slovenia and Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you performed this reserve duty were you issued uniforms and weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We kept uniforms at home and we were issued weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you issued the weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The day when the exercises started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you allowed to keep the weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did they have to be returned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the drill, when the exercise was over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you completed your compulsory military service and returned to the area, where did you work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked at the Ljubija tyres factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know a man named Dusko Tadic from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have known him since the elementary school when he held karate courses in the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever participate in that karate training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 13, 14, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since that time when you participated in the karate training, would you see Dusko Tadic in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever frequent his cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war had you ever seen him with a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen him without a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the name of any of the people whom he associated with or was friends with in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I used to see him in company with all people who had coffee bars or cafes, people who had a transportation business who had their own trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the names of some of those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jasmin Hrnic, called Jasko. I also used to see him in the company of policeman Emir Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Jasmin Hrnic do for a living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had his private trucking business.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he also known to ride motor cycles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he always rode good motor cycles, expensive, powerful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember the colour of the motor cycle that he had before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he had a Kawasaki a red one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit 269 brought up on the screen, please? Sorry, could 269 be put on the Elmo. Could we have the Elmo switched on, please? Thank you. Sir, do you recognise the people in that picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who are they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the right is Emir Karabasic and Mr. Dusko Tadic on the right side with a beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The translation, I am sorry, said, "To the right is Emir Karabasic and Mr. Dusko Tadic on the right side with a beard"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I see it, he is to the right of me as I look at it, that is Emir Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and therefore Mr. Dusko Tadic is on the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with a beard and a moustache.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, do you see the man that you know as Dusko Tadic here in this courtroom? Could you look around the courtroom please and see if you see Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please point to him and describe what he is wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He has a green suit sitting between two policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. May the record reflect that the witness identified the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The record will reflect that the witness identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Sir, before the war when did you stop working?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war we stopped working when Prijedor was occupied by the army, by the Serb one, the police, and it lasted for about two or three days, nothing worked. Then they allegedly introduced order. The army was posted at all facilities of importance. There were Serb flags hoisted up. That is how we had to move around for several days. There were checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long then after that were you able to continue working?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One day at a checkpoint manned by the Serb Army at Orlovci soldiers came in and said, "Let's see your ID cards".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the soldier came in, do you mean on the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Then those who were of Serb descent, they inferred that from their names, they were told they could go on and we who were Muslims, and others perhaps of other descent, we had to turn back, and as of that day we did not go to work any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the Kozarac area when the attack began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what day it began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do. It was Sunday, afternoon hours. It was 24th or 25th. I cannot recall the date exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when the attack began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in Kozarusa in the place Mujkanovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that at your own home or someone else's?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was with my relatives on the other side. My home is on the boundary of the Local Communes of Garevci and Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you not at your own home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we went home by day and at night we did not sleep there because as of that day when the army took over Prijedor, there were patrols and they had armed soldiers and we were afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the area around your home a predominantly Serb area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were only three Muslim homes. The rest were Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the attack began, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It began out of the blue the shelling from all types of weapons. I saw a column of vehicles coming from the direction of Prijedor. Part of that column detoured on to the road to Garevci and the other one headed in the direction of Kozarac and began shelling houses one by one. I saw my home burning, I saw it was hit, and other neighbours. Those on the road to Garevci, the tank, that one which detoured to Garevci, they also began to fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once that attack began what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What could we? There were women and children. We all felt lost. We did not know where to go, what to do. So we tried to hide in some cellars where shells could not reach, but the shells were falling all over. Every second there was a shell, one might say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you continue to move about the area over the next couple of days from place to place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point did you enter the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was in Kozarac. We thought we would be safe if we got to Kozarac, to the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Kozarac did you see Dusko Tadic in that town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the circumstances when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was the second day. We were tired, I and those, there were several boys there and men with me. We were wet because we waded through water as this was the best shield from shells and bullets and all the rest. We came across some people who told us that buses were coming and taking to Trnopolje, that there was a sort of reception centre there, although we had seen buses driving to Prijedor from the direction of Kozarac. We had made up our minds to join since we had seen those columns coming down from the direction of Kotlovici, from Mrakovici, from the top of Kozarac to the Banja Luka Road. We thought that we might perhaps join one of those columns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you in the town when you saw Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had reached that part where the school was. At that moment when I saw a tank I was behind the pharmacy, behind the building which housed the pharmacy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a tank. What did you see in the tank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw a column which was moving past the tank on the left-hand side. I recognised on the tank two persons, Dusko Tadic and Goran Borovnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Dusko Tadic or Goran Borovnica do anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see them do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the moment when he was coming off the tank people were asking something, enquiring of something. I heard a noise. I heard rough language. I heard "balija mother" cursed and what not. A young man, a boy, approached and Dule hit him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if that would be a ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber will stand in adjournment until 10 o'clock tomorrow morning. (5.30 p.m.) (The court adjourned until the following day). 19
